competitorWins: MarineTraffic is the genuine maritime-intelligence leader: 4,000+ port arrival/departure schedules with live ETAs, animated historical playback, port-call logs, vessel ownership and dimensions, 48-hour wind forecasts, fleet management, voyage planner and a mature commercial API. For compliance analysts, sanctions researchers, port professionals and fleet operators, its institutional data depth and history (up to 5 years on Enterprise) are in a different league from a generalist globe.
description: MarineTraffic (founded 2007) is the default ship-tracking platform: real-time vessel positions from thousands of AIS receivers, 4,000+ port schedules with live ETAs, vessel particulars, port-call logs and dark-shipping analysis, used by journalists and compliance analysts. Deep features sit behind paid plans. WorldEye is complementary for the general audience: free live ship tracking on a 3D globe together with flights, cameras, weather, quakes, fires and satellite imagery — no registration needed.

verdictCompetitor: Choose MarineTraffic if you need professional maritime data — port ETAs, vessel history, fleet alerts, ownership records and an API — and accept paid plans starting at $10/month.
verdictWorldEye: Choose WorldEye if you want free, signup-free ship tracking on a 3D globe together with flights, cameras, weather and satellite imagery — perfect for watching the world, not running a fleet.
whyWorldEye: Live ship tracking on a free 3D globe with no signup — no email registration, no paid tier to see the basics.
Ships are shown alongside flights, 74,229 cameras, weather, earthquakes and wildfires — one map, not one dataset.
Pro starts at $7.99/week and adds an AI analyst assistant plus OSINT toolkit for vessel research.
Satellite imagery (Pro) and cameras give context a ship dot cannot — see the port, the coast, the weather.
